asof: Settles Tue 3 Nov 2026 · written Wed 4 Nov
headline: Hot JOLTS sells the strip 1–3bp, back end leads; U7 peak at 4.535% still prices two hikes vs a one-hike Fed median.
summary: The strip sold off across the board on Tuesday, giving back Monday's back-end rally: Z6 rose 1.5bp in implied rate to 4.16%, H7 to U7 rose 1bp, and H8 through Z9 led with 2–3bp, Z9 up 3bp to 4.41%. Month-to-date the move is close to parallel, with Z6 to Z7 1–1.5bp higher and 2028–29 contracts 1.5–2bp higher. The peak is still SR3U7 at 4.535%, 58.5bp over the latest 3.95% SOFR fixing, with 12.5bp of easing priced from there to Z9. That is still about one hike more than the Fed's median and the consensus call of a December hike followed by a long hold.
drivers: Strong JOLTS reprices the labour market

September job openings jumped 333,000 to 7.523 million against about 7.10 million expected, August was revised up to 7.19 million, quits rose to 3.365 million and layoffs fell to 1.641 million. Two-year yields rose about 4.5bp to 4.63% and 10-year about 6bp to 4.95%; in SR3 Z6 rose 1.5bp and H7 to U7 1bp.
Back end cheapens into refunding and the vote

The 2028–29 contracts sold off 2–3bp as the long end lost about 5.5bp ahead of Wednesday's refunding, where many dealers expect Treasury to loosen its steady-coupon guidance and lean more on bills and shorter notes, and as midterm results shape the fiscal outlook. U7/Z8 rose 1.5bp to −9.5bp and Z7/Z8 1bp to −7bp.
Oil slides again but no longer drives the strip

Brent hit $100.80 intraday on reports the US had approved a Qatari draft accord with Iran, then pared losses after Tehran said the US response fell short; WTI settled $0.37 lower at $96.09. Cheaper oil failed to stop the selloff, so the data, not energy, set Tuesday's direction.

SOFR fixed at 3.95% on 2 November, 7bp over the 3.88% EFFR and above the 3.90% interest on reserves, with reverse repo usage near $5bn. U6 at 3.925% implied, up only 0.2bp, still sits under the fixing.
spreads: The whites were steady while the strip beyond the peak cheapened. U6/Z6 widened 1.3bp to +23.5bp, Z6/H7 narrowed 0.5bp to +20.5bp, H7/M7 held at +13bp and M7/U7 at +4bp, while U7/Z7 rose 0.5bp to −2.5bp, so the peak stays in U7. Z6/Z7 was unchanged at +35bp and Z6/M7 narrowed 0.5bp to +33.5bp, unchanged on the month. Past the peak the inversion eased: Z7/Z8 +1bp to −7bp, U7/Z8 +1.5bp to −9.5bp (0.5bp higher month-to-date) and Z8/Z9 +0.5bp to −3bp, which is still 0.5bp deeper than at end-October. Flies were quiet: H7/M7/U7 unchanged at +9bp (+0.5bp on the month) and M7/U7/Z7 down 0.5bp to +6.5bp. Week- and month-to-date changes are the same, as both run from the 30 October settle.
fed: The latest fed funds futures snapshot is Monday's: 19.7bp for the 9 December meeting (a 79% chance of a hike), 25.5bp by January, 39.9bp by March, 55.1bp by June and a 59.5bp peak by September 2027 (implied EFFR 4.475%). That is up from 17.6bp, 24bp, 37.3bp, 52.1bp and 57bp at the 30 October month-end, but below 23.4bp, 32bp, 48.6bp, 66.3bp and 72bp a week earlier and well below 30.6bp, 43.5bp, 63.4bp and a 94bp peak at end-September. SR3 agrees at the peak: 4.475% plus SOFR's 7bp premium over EFFR is about 4.545%, within 1bp of U7 at 4.535%, while Z6 at 4.16% sits about 4.5bp under the January ZQ level plus that premium. Tuesday's 2-year selloff points to slightly firmer December pricing than Monday's snapshot. The strip still prices about two more hikes; the Fed's median projects one more this year and none in 2027, Logan has called for at least two, and payrolls on Friday (about 63,000 expected) and CPI on 10 November are the last big tests before December.

ideas.title: Sell the Z6/M7 calendar spread (fade 2027 hikes)
ideas.why: Open and 4.5bp in favour at +33.5bp after narrowing 0.5bp on Tuesday, as Z6 rose 1.5bp in rate against 1bp for M7: the hot JOLTS print added to December, not to the 2027 hikes. With 13.5bp to target and 6.5bp to the stop, reward is about 2.1 times risk. Kept: the ZQ peak of 59.5bp is down from 94bp at end-September and the Fed median sees one hike, not the extra 2027 move M7 still carries.
ideas.risk: A strong payrolls print on Friday or a hot CPI on 10 November could lift the 2027 hikes and push the spread back toward +40bp.

ideas.title: Buy 2028 easing: sell Z7, buy Z8
ideas.why: Open at −7bp, 1bp against entry after rising 1bp on Tuesday as Z8's implied rate climbed 2.5bp against 1.5bp for Z7 in the back-end selloff. Only 10bp of easing is priced from Z7 to Z9; the target is 18bp away against 9bp to the stop, about 2 times. Kept at about half the core size: Tuesday was a supply-driven back-end move, not a change in the easing story, and a long-end-light refunding would help.
ideas.risk: If the refunding or midterm results add to term premium, or 2027 hikes keep coming out, the reds can flatten toward zero and push the spread through the stop.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through payrolls and refunding settlement

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 settled at 3.925% implied, up 0.2bp on the day, while the latest 3.95% SOFR fixing sits 2.5bp above it and above the 3.90% interest on reserves. Refunding auctions next week and their mid-November settlement could keep repo firm, and only U6's final week sees the December decision; revisit after the 16 November settlement.
ideas.risk: If funding pressure fades quickly, SOFR could drop back to 3.88–3.90% and leave a couple of bp on the table.

watch: Any change to the steady-coupon guidance or a tilt to bills hits the reds and funding; ADP about 68,000 and ISM services about 54.8 expected.
Jobless claims; Q3 productivity and labour costs; Fed's Hammack, Barkin and Logan
Hammack dissented for a hike in October and Logan wants at least two more, so hawkish talk would support Z6/M7 wideners.
October payrolls; Fed's Williams and Bowman
About 63,000 expected after 29,000 with unemployment at 4.2%; the main test for Z6/M7, with Williams the key voice.
Brent and the US–Iran draft accord
Qatari mediators expect replies within about 36 hours; a deal would pull 2027 hikes lower, a breakdown would push them up.
The first refunding sale, $58bn if sizes are unchanged, tests front-end demand.
The last CPI before the December meeting after 3.7% in September; it sets Z6 and the December hike odds.
ZQ prices 19.7bp, a 79% chance of a hike; the outcome sets Z6 and the whites.
